On **14 March 1958**, Washington suspended arms shipments to Cuba as relations with the regime deteriorated. As Hugh Thomas discusses in *Cuba: The Pursuit of Freedom*, American policy formed an important part of the international context of Batista’s collapse. The suspension restricted military supply and weakened the expectation that Washington would sustain his government indefinitely. Nevertheless, Batista retained substantial weapons and numerical superiority, so the measure cannot adequately explain defeat through material deprivation alone. Its psychological and diplomatic effects reinforced an existing domestic crisis. A structuralist interpretation therefore emphasizes the vulnerability created by Batista’s dependence on external recognition and support.
